Alimuzzaman Chowdhury with Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocates —For the Petitioner 
Mashuque Hossain Ahmed, Assistant Attorney-General — For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Osimuddin ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh and ors ----- opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 30-5-1993 and 8-6-1993 respectively passed by the District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 92 of 1989 setting aside and reversing the judgment and decree dated 23-2-1989 and 28-2-1989 respectively passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 should not be set aside.

2. The fact for the disposal of the Rule is as follows:

The plaintiff-opposite party i.e. Government of Bangladesh and the District Forest Officer, Dhaka Division, filed Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur for decree declaring the plaintiffs full right, title and interest in the suit land measuring 19.29 acres of CS Plot Nos. 440, 465, 475, 215, 208 of mouja Sarabo Police Station Joydevpur, District Gazipur (formerly in the District of Dhaka) and holding that the ex parte decree dated 28-12-1981 passed in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 of the Assistant Judge Court, Gazipur was fraudulent, void, collusive and without any legal effect.

3. The case of the plaintiff-opposite party was as follows:

The landed properties described in the schedule, here-in-after referred to as the suit land, originally belonged to Zaminder Rai Bahadur Arun Goure Prashad Roy Chowdhury and the Government had taken over the suit land under notification Nos. 2846 of 25-3-1953 and 16188 dated 15-12-1953 and subsequently proposed for its reservation as forest under Forest Act of 1927 by notification No. 3735(2)18-12-dated 15-9-1967. The Government had been and was still in possession of the suit land through the Forest Department of the Government. The defendant-petitioner had filed suit being Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 for declaration of his title in the suit land and it was alleged that by suppressing service of summons in collusion with the process server and other employees of the court fraudulently obtained an ex parte decree on 28-12-1981. The plaintiff-opposite parties stated that they came to know about the same in 1983. Thereupon they filed Misc. Case No. 26 of 1983 for setting aside the ex parte decree. The Misc. case was filed on 27-2-1983, which was dismissed on 16-5-1984, and because the defendant-petitioner thereafter gave an undertaking to the plaintiff that he would not come to the suit property in future no appeal was preferred against the order of dismissal of Misc. Case No. 26 of 1993. However, it was alleged that the defendant again claimed the suit land without any legal basis and only on the basis of the said ex parte decree which was alleged to have been collusively obtained by exercising fraud upon the court without the knowledge of the plaintiffs. It was further alleged that the defendant-petitioner had no right, title, interest in the suit land and he never got possession, but since the defendant started putting up claim again in March 1986, the plaintiff was constrained to file the present suit to remove the cloud on the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and prayed for a decree as stated above.

4. The defendant-petitioner contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the defendant petitioner filed Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gazipur stating that the suit property originally belonged to Zaminder Prashad Roy Chowdhury and Gouri Prashad Roy Chowdhury of Kashimpur Estate, PS Savar, District Dhaka belonging to Touzi No. 27. The CS record of rights was prepared in the name of Saroda Prashad Roy Chowdhury and others, the heirs of the said Gouri Prashad Roy Chowdhury, as owners in possession of land measuring 19.29 decimals of land of CS plot Nos. 440, 465, 575, 215 and 208 of CS Khatian No. 6 of the Mouja Sarabo. The Zamindary Estate of Kashimpur was divided into two Hissa i.e. 8 Annas 17 Gandas, 3 Karas, 1 Kraniti share and 7 Annas 2 Gondas 2 Kranti 2 Danti share, popularly known as 9 Annas and 7 Annas shareholders and they possessed the suit land. On the 12th Poush 1338 BS the defendant took settlement of the suit land from 9 Annas hissa and on the 7th day of Magh 1338 BS the defendant took settlement of the suit land also from the owners of 7 Annas hissa on payment of proper salami of Rs. 291.00 only and took delivery of physical possession of the suit land and is enjoying the same upon payment of rent. It is stated that the defendant being an illiterate cultivator could not get his name recorded during the SA khatian to the negligence of Jinnat Ali Moulavi of Saradaganj on whom the defendant trusted for the purpose. During the RS operation the defendant appeared before the officer who went to the locality for the purpose and after examining the defendant's papers of title, assured that the defendant's name would be duly recorded in the RS Khatian and subsequently gave an attested copy of the DP khatain No. 19 prepared in the name of the defendant but subsequently it transpired that the RS record had been prepared in the name of the plaintiff and the defendant's name was not entered therein. Hence the defendant filed the said Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur for a declaration of the defendant's-/16/-Annas right, title and interest in the suit land. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was decreed ex parte on 28-12-1981 not by suppression of summons which was duly served on 27-6-1981 and 29-6-1981 but in the presence of the Government Advocate Gazipur. The Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 for setting aside the said decree was filed on 27-3-1983 i.e. fourteen months thereafter with no.explanation or prayer for condonation of delay, therefore the Assistant Judge, Gazipur rejected the said Misc. case on contest on 28-3-1984 and the plaintiffs did not prefer any appeal therefrom. The defendant denied that he gave any undertaking that he would not possess the suit land after the dismissal of the Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 that is after the plaintiffs finally lost the case. The defendant after obtaining decree in the Court of Munsif, Gazipur started the Misc. case No. 124 of 1982 before the ADC (Rev), Dhaka which case was transferred from Dhaka to Gazipur and renumbered as Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 for correction of records in the name of the defendant. In the said Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 the learned CO Revenue, Gazipur twice conducted on the spot enquiry in the case land on visiting the suit land. The CO Revenue, Gazipur and after him the ADC (Rev), Gazipur also visited the suit land and made an on the spot enquiry and all the officers found the plaintiff to be in possession of the suit land. Thus found that this defendant was in possession of the suit land by construction of homestead, digging pond and that there was no Gazari tree or forest anywhere in the suit land. The local GP also gave his opinion that the suit land belonged to the defendant and not the plaintiff legally. Upon hearing this defendant and also because the plaintiff had no objection in the record being corrected in his name and as this defendant was in possession of the case land the ADC (Rev). Gazipur by his order dated 12-3-86 passed in Misc. case No. 46 of 1984 allowed correction of record in favour of this defendant. Thereafter there was again an on the spot survey and demarcation of the suit land by Government surveyor Mofizuddin, Revenue Department, Gazipur on 26-8-86 where the officers of the plaintiff and local Chairman were present, and the plaintiff's representative consented to the demarcation as per possession of this defendant. It was therefore submitted that the plaintiff had no right, title, and interest in the suit land and some other interested persons with ill motive started this false and frivolous suit although there was no Gazari tree anywhere in the suit land as falsely claimed in para 5 of the plaint as it appeared from the plaint. Further, none of the plaintiffs signed the plaint of the present suit.

5. The learned Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur upon hearing the parties and perusing the document dismissed the suit of the opposite parties with the finding that it is not a fact that the summons were suppressed in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, rather the suit was decreed in presence of the opposite parties on 28-12-1981 as it appeared from the Ext. "cha" the order sheet, and also that the plaintiff opposite parties filed the Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 which was dismissed on contest on 28-3-1984 and that as the plaintiff opposite parties did not file any appeal against the dismissal of the Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 on contest against the plaintiff opposite parties, the plaintiff opposite parties were debarred from instituting a fresh suit in respect of the same matter which was res judicata. With the said findings the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur dismissed the Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 on 23-2-1989.

6. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree dated 23-2-1989 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 23 of 1987 the plaintiff opposite parties filed Title Appeal No. 92 of 1989 in the Court of District Judge, Gazipur. The learned District Judge reversed the judgment and decree passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30-5-1993 and 8-6-1993 respectively against which the defendant petitioner has obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury, the learned Counsel appearing for the defendant-petitioner, has submitted a number of grounds whereby the appellate Court committed error of law on the face of the record leading to wrong decision and injustice on the defendant-petitioner. It is submitted that the suit land is not Gazari land and the same cannot be treated as Forest Land as had been recorded in CS Khatian No. 6 Ext. Gha in which the suit land has been described as Chala and Teek land and the schedule also supported the same. The land mentioned in the schedule of the plaint was never published in the Gazette by the Government as forest land under any provision of the Forest Act, 1927 and the learned District Judge's finding that it was forest land published in the Gazette under the provision of Forest Act, 1927 was baseless, misconceived and wrong. The only paper Ext. 1 produced by the PW 1 as notification containing some other plots than the suit plot, mere departmental notification under the provision of East Bengal Private Forest Act, 1949 and not under the provisions of Forest Act, 1927 as has been wrongly stated and observed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur. The appellate Court below committed serious error of law while reversing the finding of the trial Court that the ex parte decree having been passed upon service of summons on 28-12-1981 in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gazipur, the plaintiff opposite party preferred a Misc. case for setting aside the said ex parte decree under Order 9 rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code being Misc. case No. 26 of 1983, the restoration of the suit to its original file and number and having lost the Misc. case no. 26 of 1983 on contest on 28-3-1984 and the plaintiff-opposite party having not preferred any appeal against the said order passed in the Misc. case was debarred from filing a fresh suit between the same parties and in respect of the same property in 1987, and in not finding that the ex parte decree unless set aside also operated as res judicata in the matter. It is further submitted that a Gazette notification published on 11-7-85 and a photo copy of the same showed that the suit land was not included as forest land. A photocopy of the departmental notification dated 15-12-1953 Ext. 1 which was relied upon by the plaintiff-opposite parties was only a departmental circular and not a notification as required under section 4 of the Forest Act, 1927. It is also submitted by the learned Counsel appearing for the defendant-petitioner that the learned District Judge without considering the above facts found that the GP and the Assistant Judge had favoured the defendant petitioner who were illegally influenced by bribe and share of land. The judgment, it is submitted, is vitiated by irrelevant observation in the name of judicial notice and baseless as portion of all the concerned Government officials and the subordinate judiciary.

8. We will now consider the points raised by the learned Counsel for the defendant-petitioner. It appears from Ext. 'Gha' which is CS Khatian No. 6 that the suit land comprising of Plot No. 208, 215, 440 and 475 are described as Chala and Teek land. There is no mention that any of the lands was Gazari land. This has not been disputed by the plaintiffs. If these lands, were not forest land then they could not have been declared as land for reserve forest. It is the plaintiffs case that the suit land was taken over by the Government under State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by Notification No. 2846 of 25-3-1953 and Notification No. 16188 of 15-12-53 and subsequently for reservation as forest under Forest Act, 1927. If it was forest land then section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act would not apply, as forest land vested in the Government without any notification of all CS recorded forest land vested in the Government as per proviso to section 20 of the Forest Act, 1927. If on the other hand the plaintiffs claim that the suit land was Gazari land is accepted, then giving notice under section 4 of Forest Act 1927 and the procedure laid down from section 4 to section 20 of the said Act has to be complied with. In the instant case although the appellate Court has referred to Gazette notification there is nothing on record to show that there was any Gazette notification under section 4 which requires there has to be a notification in the official Gazette. Ext. 1 upon which the plaintiffs have relied is a departmental notice which cannot be said to be an official notification as envisaged in section 4 of the Forest Act, 1927. In the case of Hazi Nurul Islam vs. Serajul Islam and ors. reported in 1984 BLD (AD) 36 the Appellate Division while considering the fact of Government circular in respect of principles of lease of Government fisheries held that the Matter did not have any statutory force nor were they published in the official Gazette for general information to the members of the public, so as to saddle them with the knowledge of the principles regulating the leasing out of fisheries. At best, this offered a guideline for the use of the officers of the department without prescribing any sanction against the violation of the principles contained therein as far as the members of the public are concerned.

<u>9. In the present case Ext. 1 appears to be nothing but a departmental notification which could not affect the right of the public. Further the notification was not published in the official Gazette as specifically required under section 4 and section 6 of the Forest Act, 1927. The appellate Court obviously came to an error in holding that a Gazette notification was published in respect of the suit land although no such Gazette notification appears in the record filed by the plaintiff. A photocopy Gazette notification was filed by the defendant which was published in 1985 and the suit land does not appear to be included in the said notification under section 6 of the Forest Act, 1927.</u>

<u>10. It appears from the record that the defendant filed suit being Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 for declaration of his title in the suit property. In the said suit the plaintiff opposite parties as defendant filed a petition praying for time to file written statement on the ground stated therein. The learned Asstt Judge, Gazipur rejected the petition on the ground that it could not be considered at that stage. The suit was therefore decreed ex parte in favour of the defendant-petitioner on 23-1-1982. Thereafter the plaintiff opposite party filed a petition under Order 9 rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code being Misc. case No. 26 of 1983. The said Misc. case was dismissed on contest on 28-3-1984. It would thus appear that the plaintiff-opposite party's lawyer being present and having filed a petition for time had full knowledge of the ex parte decree when it was passed on 23-1-82. The Asstt. Judge took this into consideration while dismissing the Misc. case No. 26 of 1983 on the ground that it had been filed 14 months after the ex parte decree which was beyond the limitation period prescribed by law. It thus appears clear that it was found on contest that there had been no suppression of notice on the plaintiff-opposite party nor any fraud committed in the proceedings of the court. It also appears that no revision/appeal was filed by the plaintiff opposite party against the dismissal of Misc. case No. 26 of 1983. After a long lapse of 4 years the plaintiff-filed the present suit being Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 for setting aside the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981. It was alleged by the plaintiff that the ex parte decree was obtained collusively. The learned Asstt. Judge dismissed the suit, inter alia, holding that the ex parte decree had been passed with the knowledge of the present plaintiff and the Misc. case filed by the plaintiff having been dismissed on contest and there being no appeal or revision filed against that judgment and order of dismissal under Order 9 rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code that the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was res judicata under section 11 of the CPC as subject matter of the present suit was the sane and between the same parties. The appellate Court has alleged bribery and collusion between the defendant petitioner, the GP and the trial Court, but without any evidence in support thereof. He has presumed that the ex parte decree was obtained by fraud by bribing officers in the department of Forest, the GP and also the Court. He has also presumed that the delay in filing Misc. case under Order 9 rule 13 and then not filing any revision or appeal against the order of dismissal of the Misc. case was also obtained by bribery and collusion to have a share on the suit land. These observations appear to be the feelings of the appellate Court without any legal basis or evidence. They are presumptive. The authorities concerned the GP and the Assistant Judge were not parties in the suit and, as such, the observation of bribery and collusion against them is uncalled for. In the case of Mrida Begum and others vs. Moulavi Md. Hasan and others reported in 10 BLD 1990 page 334 it was held that fraud cannot be imputed against authorities exercising judicial function either as Court or Tribunal. We have noted that there was nothing to show that the plaintiffs in the suit were prevented from appearing in Title Suit No. 860 of 81 which was decreed ex parte with full knowledge of the plaintiffs’ lawyer who had applied for time for filing written statement, but was rejected. In the absence of any fraud committed in the proceeding before the trial Court the ex parte decree unless reversed is res judicata to subsequent suit filed on the same subject and between same parties.</u>

11. We may discuss some cases on the subject. In the case of Rangalal Sutradhar vs. Satish Chandra reported in 11 DLR (1959) 376; it was held that as ex parte decree cannot be re-opened in a later action brought to set aside on the ground of fraud simply because the claim decreed ex parte was false. The only ground on which a decree in a previous suit can be successfully challenged in a suit for setting aside the decree is that the plaintiff was prevented by the fraud of the decree holder in the previous suit before the court. In the instant case that does not appear to be the position.

12. In the case of Kumar Begum Roy vs. Panna Debi and others reported in 1982 BLD (AD) 54 the Appellate Division held that fresh suit for achieving the same result by adopting indirect method is not permissible order of dismissal for default passed by the Calcutta High Court on September 1, 1949 in a suit filed by the plaintiff in 1944. The Appellate Division held as follows:

"By filing the present suit the appellant has merely adopted an indirect method to achieve in her suit filed in the Calcutta High Court. What she failed to achieve directly, she now wants to achieve indirectly. Law does not allow it to be done. It also appears that in the Calcutta High Court she did not proceed with the suit which was allowed to be dismissed for default on account of her non-appearance. She did not take any further step to have the orders of dismissal for default set aside. Under the provisions of Order 9, rule 9 CPC the present suit is barred."

In the instant case there was ex parte decree against which the plaintiff filed a Misc. case which was dismissed on contest. The plaintiff did not take any step by way of revision/appeal against the said dismissal order and instead has filed the present suit alleging collusion. This is a similar case when the plaintiff having failed to achieve directly by filing the Misc. case under Order 9 rule 9 is trying by filing the present suit for setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground of collusion.

13. In the case of Khan Sahed vs. Abdul Khaleque Sowdagar, Proprietor, Chittagong Rice Mills & Co. vs. Majutar Rahman Khan, reported in 12 PLR 421, it was held by Division Bench of the High Court as follows :

"(1) An ex parte decree can be set aside by new action, when the Court passing it had been misled by fraud. It must be actual and positive fraud relating to the proceeding of the court, a premeditated and intentional contrivance to keep the parties and the court in ignorance of the real and material facts of the case in order to obtain decree by that contrivance.

(2) Falsity of claim by itself is no ground for setting aside decrees on the ground of fraud nor perjured evidence, by which the decree might have been procured, can be ground for setting aside the ex parte decree in a new action.

(3) A decree obtained through suppression of material facts or on perjured evidence cannot be a ground for maintainability of a separate suit setting aside the decree as these omissions do not prevent the relevant party from appearing and placing his case before the Court."

In the case before us there is nothing to show that trial Court had been misled by fraud or that there has been actual and positive fraud relating to the proceeding of the Court or a premeditated or intentional contrivance to keep the parties and the court in ignorance of the real and material facts in order to obtain decree by that contrivance. Nothing of the kind appears to have been found by the appellate Court. There is simply finding on presumption that the decree was obtained by bribery and corruption without evidence.

14. In the case of Bangladesh vs. Rahimuddin reported in 1987 BLD 307 the question was whether ex parte decision in a former suit between the parties over the same matter will operate as res jusdicata. In the former suit the issue regarding acquisition of customary right of pasturage over the suit land by the plaintiffs was raised and finally decided though the suit was decreed ex parte. It was held that the decision of the former suit will operate as res judicata. The decree even if ex parte will operate as res judicata. A Single Bench of the High Court Division in the case observed:

"Now the question that arises for consideration is whether ex parte decree passed in OC Suit No. 55 of 1949 can operate as res judicata and the defendants are estopped from raising the same question that is, whether plaintiffs acquired customary right of pasturage in the suit land. In the former suit this issue was raised and finally decided though the suit was decreed ex parte. Therefore, decision of the former suit will operate as res judicata inasmuch as the pleadings and the prayer made in the former suit gave express notice to the defendant appellant Government that the question would or might be decided. A decree even if ex parte will operate as res judicata in respect of all grounds on defendants against actual claim in the suit as also matter insistent in the suit that claim which might or ought to have been raised. In the absence of fraud or irregularity a decree obtained ex parte is binding for all purposes as contested decree."

<u>15. In the instant case as pointed out, the ex parte decree was not obtained by fraud and the Misc. case under Order 9 rule 13 filed by the plaintiff was also dismissed on contest. Therefore the ex parte decree in the instant case would operate as res judicata on the present suit.</u>

16. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner pointed out that it appears from the record that the defendant-petitioner had paid rent and has referred to Exhibits on record. He has argued that once the Government accepts the rent it is estopped to challenge the title in support. In support of his contention he has referred to the case of Bangladesh vs. Askar Ali reported in BCR 1988 (HCD) 179. In the said case land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs as tenants under the order of SDO. The Tahsilder accepted rent of the suit land from the plaintiffs and granted rent receipts since the plaintiffs were in possession of 9 bighas of the suit land. So it was held that obviously the claims of the plaintiffs were partially admitted by the defendants. Once the record of right was corrected and Government accepted rent from the plaintiff for the entire suit property, the Government is estopped to challenge the title of the plaintiff and the plaintiff had good title in the suit land.

<u>17. In the instant case the Government having accepted the rent from the defendant petitioner it was estopped from challenging the title of the defendant petitioner. The appellate Court without any basis held that the officer concerned was corrupt and therefore did not consider the facts disclosed in exhibit "ঝ" The said exhibit showed that the Revenue Officer, Gazipur had visited the suit land and found the defendant-petitioner to be in possession of the suit land and had constructed houses thereon. On enquiry it was found that the suit land was in possession of the defendant with a house and that there was no Gazari land. The Department of Forest was not present in spite of several notices to them. The ADC (Rev.) thereafter directed payment of rent of the suit land by the defendant petitioner. In doing so it accepted the title and interest of the defendant petitioner.</u>

18. In the light of my above observation I must hold that the appellate Court committed error in law leading to wrong decision and causing injustice to the defendant petitioner.

19. In the result the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 30-5-1993 and 8-6-1993 passed by the District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 92 of 1989 setting aside and reversing the judgment and decree dated 23-2-1989 and 28-2-1989 respectively passed by the Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 is set aside. The judgment and decree dated 23-2-89 and 28-2-89 passed by the Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 is hereby restored.

End.
